description: We are Tech Bees, a two-member team interested in AI, Machine Learning, data analysis, and space exploration. We aim to build a practical and innovative solution for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by combining technology, creativity, and teamwork.
summary:
FLARE Intelligence is an AI-powered research and exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It focuses on making space science and microgravity combustion research more accessible through interactive visualizations, scientific information, and AI-assisted exploration.

Using NASA's Burning and Suppression of Solids II (BASS-II) investigation as a primary combustion research resource, the platform helps users explore how materials ignite, burn, spread flames, and extinguish under microgravity conditions. It also provides access to broader NASA mission information to connect scientific exploration with future space missions.

By combining Python-based data processing, interactive analytics, and an AI research assistant powered by large language models, FLARE Intelligence aims to transform complex research information into understandable insights.

The project supports scientific learning and exploration of fire-safety considerations for future spacecraft and human space missions.
details:
FLARE Intelligence

AI-Powered Microgravity Combustion Research & Space Mission Insights

1. Introduction

FLARE Intelligence is an AI-powered scientific research and exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The project focuses on making NASA research, microgravity combustion experiments, and space mission information easier to explore through an interactive and intelligent web application.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity compared with normal gravity. Understanding ignition, flame spread, burning behaviour, and extinction is important for investigating fire-safety challenges in spacecraft and future human space missions.

2. The Problem

Scientific research is often distributed across technical reports, experimental datasets, and mission documentation. Exploring and understanding these resources can be challenging for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

Microgravity combustion research is particularly important because conventional Earth-based assumptions about flame behaviour may not fully describe fire in space environments.

3. Our Solution

FLARE Intelligence brings scientific research exploration, interactive data analysis, and AI-assisted information retrieval into one platform.

The application uses NASA's Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) investigation as a primary combustion research resource. It also presents broader NASA mission information as supporting space exploration context.

4. Main Features

Scientific Research Exploration

Explore NASA research resources and scientific information related to microgravity combustion and space exploration.

Flame Behaviour Analytics

Examine available experimental measurements and explore combustion characteristics through interactive visualizations.

Experiment Comparison

Compare available experimental information and investigate differences in documented combustion conditions and findings.

AI Research Assistant

Interact with a large language model to explore research questions and obtain AI-assisted explanations of scientific information.

Mission Insights

Explore NASA mission information, including relevant planetary exploration and space science missions.

Findings and Evidence

Organize research observations and supporting information to help users distinguish documented evidence from AI-assisted interpretation.

5. NASA Research Foundation

The primary combustion research resource is NASA's BASS-II investigation, which studies ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels in microgravity.

The investigation examines variables including airflow velocity, oxygen concentration, and fuel sample geometry. Its research contributes to understanding spacecraft fire safety and the development of combustion models.

Other NASA mission pages are used as contextual references where included in the application. They are not presented as microgravity combustion datasets.

6. Technology Stack

  • Python — application logic and scientific processing
  • Streamlit — interactive web application
  • Pandas — data manipulation
  • Plotly — interactive scientific visualizations
  • Groq API — large language model integration
  • Llama 3.3 70B — AI-assisted research interaction
  • edge-tts — text-to-speech functionality using neural voices
  • Google Fonts — Bricolage Grotesque and Source Serif 4
  • GitHub — source code management and project repository

7. Innovation

FLARE Intelligence combines scientific research exploration, data visualization, AI-assisted question answering, and space mission information in a single accessible platform.

Its goal is to reduce the effort required to navigate complex scientific resources and make research information easier to understand.

The platform emphasizes research accessibility, interactive exploration, and the importance of evidence-based scientific interpretation.

8. Intended Impact

The project aims to support students, researchers, and space-science enthusiasts in exploring microgravity combustion research.

It can help users understand why combustion behaves differently in space and why further investigation is important for future spacecraft and habitat safety.

The application is a research and educational platform. It is not a certified spacecraft fire-risk prediction, detection, or suppression system.

9. Development Team

Team Techbees consists of two members who collaborated on research, application development, data exploration, AI integration, interface design, and project documentation.
